question: May test_cairn_resolves_from_powershell.py change how its teeth report off Windows (both raise UNRAN through one guard and print '  FAIL <tooth>: ...UNRAN...') while its two clauses stay word for word?
why_it_blocks: rung 4 of the seal-red ladder refuses the proof's new bytes without an answered question; the Linux red seal holds bin's component_color red and eb1b46bed3d8 and 69075b0e8212 at PROVED
answer: Yes. The two clauses (cairn resolves to bin/cairn.cmd; a read-only verb matches Git Bash) and every Windows assertion are unchanged; only the off-Windows reading changes, from a plain RED to not-run. That is the reading the tester's not-run rule already implements (ticket 64ae0df3f1f3, cairn/devices/tester/device.py unran_only), and the outline's own form of it (9.4.8.1: a tooth a box cannot run reads not-run, never red). Measured on akiendelllinux 2026-11-22: the new bytes print FAIL ... UNRAN for both teeth, and unran_only returns both, so a Linux reseal writes no seal.
